(iii) \(\text{CH}_4\)
Calculate the mass per cent of different elements present in sodium sulphate \(\left(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\right)\).
Determine the empirical formula of an oxide of iron, which has 69.9% iron and 30.1% dioxygen by mass.

Calculate the amount of carbon dioxide that could be produced when
(i) 1 mole of carbon is burnt in air.

Calculate the amount of carbon dioxide that could be produced when
(ii) 1 mole of carbon is burnt in \(16\,\text{g}\) of dioxygen.

Calculate the amount of carbon dioxide that could be produced when
(iii) 2 moles of carbon are burnt in \(16\,\text{g}\) of dioxygen.

Calculate the mass of sodium acetate \(\left(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}\right)\) required to make \(500\,\text{mL}\) of \(0.375\) molar aqueous solution. Molar mass of sodium acetate is \(82.0245\,\text{g mol}^{-1}\).
Calculate the concentration of nitric acid in moles per litre in a sample which has a density, \(1.41\,\text{g mL}^{-1}\) and the mass per cent of nitric acid in it being 69%.
How much copper can be obtained from \(100\,\text{g}\) of copper sulphate \(\left(\text{CuSO}_4\right)\)?
Determine the molecular formula of an oxide of iron, in which the mass per cent of iron and oxygen are 69.9 and 30.1, respectively.
_note: The stem gives no molar mass, so strictly only the empirical formula is determinable; the book's own Ex 1.3 asks the same data for the empirical formula. Transcribed as printed.

Dinitrogen and dihydrogen react with each other to produce ammonia according to the following chemical equation:

\(\text{N}_2(g) + \text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(g)\)

(i) Calculate the mass of ammonia produced if \(2.00 \times 10^{3}\,\text{g}\) dinitrogen reacts with \(1.00 \times 10^{3}\,\text{g}\) of dihydrogen.
(ii) Will any of the two reactants remain unreacted?
(iii) If yes, which one and what would be its mass?
_note: The printed equation \(\text{N}_2(g) + \text{H}_2(g) \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3(g)\) is NOT balanced — it needs \(3\text{H}_2\). Transcribed exactly as printed; the calculation requires the balanced equation.
